executedBy: agent via MCP for Blender (owner-authorized, telemetry consent off)
method: The six authoring/check python files were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com into a temporary staging directory on the Blender host (sha256-verified against the repository copies before running), then blender_authoring_check.run_checks(staging) was executed inside the live Blender session. Staging was deleted and the temporary listener stopped after the run; the owner's open scene was never saved and its fingerprints were asserted unchanged by the check itself.
findings: First execution attempt failed with AssertionError (cancelled export reported as success) because the long-running Blender session had stale authoring modules cached in sys.modules from an earlier era; purging the cache and re-running passed. The stale-module purge is now part of blender_authoring_check.py so future live runs are immune.

The genuine exports replaced the surgered files in this milestone; the prior values are preserved below.
isolationAssertions: Foreign scene object/material/selection/active-object fingerprints unchanged; two generations without data-block leaks per asset; forced export failure and cancelled export both rejected; every node name carries its asset prefix; per-asset and total size limits hold.
